work.title: The Life and Death of King Richard the Second
work.author: William Shakespeare

scene.label: Act 5, Scene 1
scene.title: SCENE I. London. A street leading to the Tower.
scene.location: London. A street leading to the Tower.

lines.text: This way the King will come. This is the way
lines.plainText: This way the King will come This is the way

lines.text: To Julius Caesar's ill-erected tower,
lines.plainText: To Julius Caesar's illerected tower

lines.text: To whose flint bosom my condemned lord
lines.plainText: To whose flint bosom my condemned lord

lines.text: Is doomed a prisoner by proud Bolingbroke.
lines.plainText: Is doomed a prisoner by proud Bolingbroke

lines.text: Here let us rest, if this rebellious earth
lines.plainText: Here let us rest if this rebellious earth

lines.text: Have any resting for her true king's queen.
lines.plainText: Have any resting for her true king's queen

lines.text: Join not with grief, fair woman, do not so,
lines.plainText: Join not with grief fair woman do not so

lines.text: To make my end too sudden. Learn, good soul,
lines.plainText: To make my end too sudden Learn good soul

lines.text: To think our former state a happy dream,
lines.plainText: To think our former state a happy dream

lines.text: From which awaked, the truth of what we are
lines.plainText: From which awaked the truth of what we are

lines.text: Shows us but this. I am sworn brother, sweet,
lines.plainText: Shows us but this I am sworn brother sweet

lines.text: To grim Necessity, and he and I
lines.plainText: To grim Necessity and he and I

lines.text: Will keep a league till death. Hie thee to France,
lines.plainText: Will keep a league till death Hie thee to France

lines.text: And cloister thee in some religious house.
lines.plainText: And cloister thee in some religious house

lines.text: Our holy lives must win a new world's crown,
lines.plainText: Our holy lives must win a new world's crown

lines.text: Which our profane hours here have thrown down.
lines.plainText: Which our profane hours here have thrown down

lines.text: What, is my Richard both in shape and mind
lines.plainText: What is my Richard both in shape and mind

lines.text: Transformed and weakened! Hath Bolingbroke
lines.plainText: Transformed and weakened Hath Bolingbroke

lines.text: Deposed thine intellect? Hath he been in thy heart?
lines.plainText: Deposed thine intellect Hath he been in thy heart

lines.text: The lion dying thrusteth forth his paw
lines.plainText: The lion dying thrusteth forth his paw

lines.text: And wounds the earth, if nothing else, with rage
lines.plainText: And wounds the earth if nothing else with rage

lines.text: To be o'erpowered; and wilt thou, pupil-like,
lines.plainText: To be o'erpowered and wilt thou pupillike

lines.text: Take the correction mildly, kiss the rod,
lines.plainText: Take the correction mildly kiss the rod

lines.text: And fawn on rage with base humility,
lines.plainText: And fawn on rage with base humility

lines.text: Which art a lion and the king of beasts?
lines.plainText: Which art a lion and the king of beasts

lines.text: A king of beasts, indeed! If aught but beasts,
lines.plainText: A king of beasts indeed If aught but beasts

lines.text: I had been still a happy king of men.
lines.plainText: I had been still a happy king of men

lines.text: Good sometimes queen, prepare thee hence for France.
lines.plainText: Good sometimes queen prepare thee hence for France

lines.text: Think I am dead, and that even here thou tak'st,
lines.plainText: Think I am dead and that even here thou tak'st

lines.text: As from my death-bed, thy last living leave.
lines.plainText: As from my deathbed thy last living leave

lines.text: In winter's tedious nights sit by the fire
lines.plainText: In winter's tedious nights sit by the fire

lines.text: With good old folks, and let them tell thee tales
lines.plainText: With good old folks and let them tell thee tales

lines.text: Of woeful ages long ago betid;
lines.plainText: Of woeful ages long ago betid

lines.text: And ere thou bid good night, to quit their griefs,
lines.plainText: And ere thou bid good night to quit their griefs

lines.text: Tell thou the lamentable tale of me,
lines.plainText: Tell thou the lamentable tale of me

lines.text: And send the hearers weeping to their beds.
lines.plainText: And send the hearers weeping to their beds

lines.text: For why, the senseless brands will sympathize
lines.plainText: For why the senseless brands will sympathize

lines.text: The heavy accent of thy moving tongue,
lines.plainText: The heavy accent of thy moving tongue

lines.text: And in compassion weep the fire out;
lines.plainText: And in compassion weep the fire out

lines.text: And some will mourn in ashes, some coal-black,
lines.plainText: And some will mourn in ashes some coalblack

lines.text: For the deposing of a rightful king.
lines.plainText: For the deposing of a rightful king

lines.text: My lord, the mind of Bolingbroke is changed.
lines.plainText: My lord the mind of Bolingbroke is changed

lines.text: You must to Pomfret, not unto the Tower.
lines.plainText: You must to Pomfret not unto the Tower

lines.text: And, madam, there is order ta'en for you:
lines.plainText: And madam there is order ta'en for you

lines.text: With all swift speed you must away to France.
lines.plainText: With all swift speed you must away to France

lines.text: Northumberland, thou ladder wherewithal
lines.plainText: Northumberland thou ladder wherewithal

lines.text: The mounting Bolingbroke ascends my throne,
lines.plainText: The mounting Bolingbroke ascends my throne

lines.text: The time shall not be many hours of age
lines.plainText: The time shall not be many hours of age

lines.text: More than it is ere foul sin, gathering head,
lines.plainText: More than it is ere foul sin gathering head

lines.text: Shall break into corruption. Thou shalt think,
lines.plainText: Shall break into corruption Thou shalt think

lines.text: Though he divide the realm and give thee half
lines.plainText: Though he divide the realm and give thee half

lines.text: It is too little, helping him to all.
lines.plainText: It is too little helping him to all

lines.text: And he shall think that thou, which knowst the way
lines.plainText: And he shall think that thou which knowst the way

lines.text: To plant unrightful kings, wilt know again,
lines.plainText: To plant unrightful kings wilt know again

lines.text: Being ne'er so little urged, another way
lines.plainText: Being ne'er so little urged another way

lines.text: To pluck him headlong from the usurped throne.
lines.plainText: To pluck him headlong from the usurped throne

lines.text: The love of wicked men converts to fear,
lines.plainText: The love of wicked men converts to fear

lines.text: That fear to hate, and hate turns one or both
lines.plainText: That fear to hate and hate turns one or both

lines.text: To worthy danger and deserved death.
lines.plainText: To worthy danger and deserved death

lines.text: My guilt be on my head, and there an end.
lines.plainText: My guilt be on my head and there an end

lines.text: Take leave and part, for you must part forthwith.
lines.plainText: Take leave and part for you must part forthwith

lines.text: Doubly divorced! Bad men, you violate
lines.plainText: Doubly divorced Bad men you violate

lines.text: A twofold marriage, 'twixt my crown and me,
lines.plainText: A twofold marriage 'twixt my crown and me

lines.text: And then betwixt me and my married wife.
lines.plainText: And then betwixt me and my married wife

lines.text: Let me unkiss the oath 'twixt thee and me;
lines.plainText: Let me unkiss the oath 'twixt thee and me

lines.text: And yet not so, for with a kiss 'twas made.
lines.plainText: And yet not so for with a kiss 'twas made

lines.text: Part us, Northumberland: I towards the north,
lines.plainText: Part us Northumberland I towards the north

lines.text: Where shivering cold and sickness pines the clime;
lines.plainText: Where shivering cold and sickness pines the clime

lines.text: My wife to France, from whence set forth in pomp,
lines.plainText: My wife to France from whence set forth in pomp

lines.text: She came adorned hither like sweet May,
lines.plainText: She came adorned hither like sweet May

lines.text: Sent back like Hallowmas or short'st of day.
lines.plainText: Sent back like Hallowmas or short'st of day

lines.text: And must we be divided? Must we part?
lines.plainText: And must we be divided Must we part

lines.text: Ay, hand from hand, my love, and heart from heart.
lines.plainText: Ay hand from hand my love and heart from heart

lines.text: Banish us both, and send the King with me.
lines.plainText: Banish us both and send the King with me

lines.text: That were some love, but little policy.
lines.plainText: That were some love but little policy

lines.text: Then whither he goes, thither let me go.
lines.plainText: Then whither he goes thither let me go

lines.text: So two, together weeping, make one woe.
lines.plainText: So two together weeping make one woe

lines.text: Weep thou for me in France, I for thee here;
lines.plainText: Weep thou for me in France I for thee here

lines.text: Better far off than near, be ne'er the near.
lines.plainText: Better far off than near be ne'er the near

lines.text: Go, count thy way with sighs, I mine with groans.
lines.plainText: Go count thy way with sighs I mine with groans

lines.text: So longest way shall have the longest moans.
lines.plainText: So longest way shall have the longest moans

lines.text: Twice for one step I'll groan, the way being short,
lines.plainText: Twice for one step I'll groan the way being short

lines.text: And piece the way out with a heavy heart.
lines.plainText: And piece the way out with a heavy heart

lines.text: Come, come, in wooing sorrow let's be brief,
lines.plainText: Come come in wooing sorrow let's be brief

lines.text: Since, wedding it, there is such length in grief.
lines.plainText: Since wedding it there is such length in grief

lines.text: One kiss shall stop our mouths, and dumbly part;
lines.plainText: One kiss shall stop our mouths and dumbly part

lines.text: Thus give I mine, and thus take I thy heart.
lines.plainText: Thus give I mine and thus take I thy heart

lines.text: Give me mine own again; 'twere no good part
lines.plainText: Give me mine own again 'twere no good part

lines.text: To take on me to keep and kill thy heart.
lines.plainText: To take on me to keep and kill thy heart

lines.text: We make woe wanton with this fond delay:
lines.plainText: We make woe wanton with this fond delay

lines.text: Once more, adieu. The rest let sorrow say.
lines.plainText: Once more adieu The rest let sorrow say
